oneLine: Close to the bar but not there yet. Every static canonical shot is clean, restrained and AoE IV-legible: capacity sits on the chips, the selected-group view is decluttered, the objectives are consistent and the menu and debrief look shipped. At the siren, the one beat that matters most, the off-screen pointers still float inward under the roster instead of sitting on the screen edge, and the two of them overlap ('WES' cut off by the '10' pill) for about 2 s. The coach line also asks you to open locked shelters when none are locked.
strengths: S2, S4 and S4b at 1600x900 have no marker overlaps. Shelters now show capacity on compact chips ('0/22', '0/40'). Groups show count + ETA chips coloured by status, and names appear only on near chips (S4: '0/26 AVENUE', '22 29s ON TIME · CAFÉ TERRACE'). This is close to the AoE IV pin discipline.

The selected-group view (ux/ux-1-route-preview.png) is fixed. Only the hovered shelter ('0/22 37s 22 FREE', white outline) and the current target ('0/26 ETA 180s 4 PLACES LEFT') get full chips. The other shelters are compact ETA chips tinted red or green by fit ('0/40 246s', 'LOCKED 361s'), and the roster row is highlighted. A first-time player can read it in seconds.

The red-alert module (S4, S4b, C2) is elegant and unmissable: צבע אדום in correct Hebrew, the English line, the large countdown, the draining bar and 'IN PROTECTED SPACES 0 / 92'. The toast has its own slot under the alert ('Opening West shelter · crew on site in 5 s', ux-2), and the opening shelters get amber '5s' chips. The banner and toast system is at CoH3 level.
Objective state is consistent. In S7 all four are ticked ('No impacts in Arad · none', 'Hold until the all-clear · done') and they match the debrief.

The menu (M0-menu) and debrief (S8) read like a shipped game: large display type, Hebrew חומת ברזל, a mono date line, keycap hints, a historical framing footnote, and an after-action report with intercept bars by layer and an 'In history' coda.
The radar now has an Arad inset (S2, S4, ux-2) with readable shelter squares and coloured group dots. That makes it usable at town scale, which WARNO / Broken Arrow-style minimaps also manage.

tools/ux-test.mjs re-run by the critic passes: every check PASS, UX-TEST PASS (pad popup build, G7 to S7 with hover preview, siren unlock of S1/S5 via 'marker full', roster pan, 0/92 exposed at t=235, no console errors). report.json and capture.json show 0 console errors in every shot and clip.

issues.text: In C2, from early warning (f00012) through the siren (f00040–f00056, t≈158–162), the 'WEST' locked-shelter pointer and the late '10' group pointer are not on the viewport edge. They sit in world space at about x=120–230, y=260, just under the roster panel. At the siren they overlap each other: the '10' pill covers the end of 'WEST', so it reads 'WES'. Both chevrons point up into the roster's corner rather than toward the targets. A player reads them as a broken world label on a building. AoE IV and CoH3 keep off-screen alerts flush to the viewport border, spaced apart, with the arrow pointing at the target.
issues.fix: src/hud/index.js placeEdges() lines 546–549. When the border hit is on the left or right edge (kx <= ky) and it lands inside a panel, keep x on the border and slide y past the panel (y = o[3] + 16 or o[1] - 16, whichever is nearer the projected y). The current code moves x inward to o[2]+16 instead. Do the mirror case for top and bottom hits. Then run a simple collision pass over the edge pills: push each one along the border by its height + 4 px when it overlaps an earlier pill or any placed marker rect, or merge pointers that share a direction into one pill ('[lock] W · [people] 10'). Recompute the chevron angle from the final pill position to the target's projected direction.

issues.text: In S4, S4b and C2 after t≈163, every shelter is already open (autopilot), but the coach line still says 'Click a locked shelter to open it · click a group, then a shelter, to reroute'. This misleads a first-time player about what to do next. The CoH3 and AoE IV hint strips only show actions that are available right now.
issues.fix: In src/hud/index.js where the hint text is chosen in the alert phase, branch on sim.shelters.some(s => s.locked && s.opening <= 0). With no locked shelters, show the late/tight-group variant ('All shelters open · reroute amber or red groups: click a group, then a shelter'). With every group on time, hide the hint or show 'Everyone is on time · hold'.

issues.text: Markers whose feet sit just outside a panel get squeezed against its border. In C2 f00012 and f00056, the Lookout lock chip sits right next to the roster's top-right corner (x≈220, y≈60–78). In S4 the '1/20' Nevatim/pad chip and its diamond touch the roster edge at x≈257. They read as part of the panel rather than the world. Markers whose foot is under a panel are hidden entirely, so the Lookout lock at the siren has no on-screen marker or edge pointer, only the roster's red 'lock' text.
issues.fix: placeMarkers(): add a 10–12 px margin around the obstacle rects for labels only (the feet keep the current rect). For a trouble marker (locked at alert, late group) with m.under, route it to placeEdges() as if off-screen, so it gets an edge pill on the border next to the panel. Do not hide it.

issues.text: At default and wide zoom (S4b, ux-2), each group's chip and its target shelter's chip often sit side by side with two feet a few pixels apart ('0/22' diamond plus '10 23s' ring, '0/28' plus '12 11s'). Which group is heading where is only implied by proximity. There is no faint route line unless a group is selected. CoH3 shows move intent with subtle ground lines.
issues.fix: In the route canvas during alert, draw every unsheltered group's current route at about 20% alpha, 1 px, status-coloured. Keep the full-strength dashed route for the selected or hovered group only.

issues.text: HUD timing in capture.json is 28.5 ms on the sampled C2 frame and 8 ms in S4b's report.json. Both were taken on a heavily contended 2-CPU box (another builder's capture, regress and audio-render were running), so they are not conclusive. The builder's own measure, p95 1.8 ms against a 1 ms budget, still says the per-frame marker and edge placement is over budget. On the menu, the key-hint row wraps and leaves 'C cinematic' orphaned on a second line. The debrief's 'Intercepted in your sector · 55 of 65' and the layer bars (sum 79) use different denominators without saying so.
issues.fix: Run placeMarkers/placeEdges at most every other frame when the camera matrix is unchanged, and use a uniform grid for hits() instead of a linear scan. Menu: widen .keys or allow the hint row to use the 650 px text column width with flex-wrap balanced (or drop the 'C cinematic' hint to the intro card). Debrief: label the bars 'all intercepts tonight' or show '/ total' per layer.

benchmarkNotes: AoE IV: the panel hierarchy (clock and budget top-left, roster under it, objectives top-right, air defence and radar bottom-left, command bar bottom-centre) and the icon-plus-number pins now meet the AoE IV bar in every static shot, and the selected-group routing view is as legible as AoE IV's target tags. CoH3: the alert module, toast slot and amber 'opening' chips match CoH3's objective and notification polish. The off-screen pointers at the siren still don't: CoH3 pins them to the screen border and never lets two overlap. Iron Harvest: restraint is good (thin hairlines, dim feed, siren-tinted vignette), and the menu and title type feel cinematic. WARNO / Broken Arrow: the battery ammo bars and the radar with its new Arad inset are believable air-defence UI. Overall it is close to the reference bar, with 2–3 visible gaps. The clearest is an overlapping, mis-anchored pointer pair at the most important beat, the siren, which is more than a nitpick. That keeps it at 7. Fixing placeEdges() and the stale coach line would likely make it an 8.
